title: Injectable hydrogel electrodes as conduction highways to restore native pacing.
result: Injectable hydrogel electrode restored native-like QRS morphology and faster activation wavefronts than single-point pacing in a pig model; feasibility of a new pacing modality, not a cardiology software study.

title: Measuring Heart Rate in Freely Moving Mice.
result: Lab protocol for implanted-ECG heart rate measurement in mice with a MATLAB GUI for data processing; no comparative usability or performance figures reported.

title: Estimating the Severity of Obstructive Sleep Apnea Using ECG, Respiratory Effort and Neural Networks.
venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
metric: Sleep-staging agreement and AHI estimation accuracy vs. polysomnography
result: Four-class sleep staging kappa 0.69 vs. PSG; AHI estimation ICC 0.91; high diagnostic performance across OSA severity thresholds.

title: Usability of myocardial work parameters to demonstrate subclinical myocardial involvement in normotensive individuals with exaggerated hypertensive response in treadmill exercise testing.
metric: Echocardiographic myocardial work parameters between hypertensive-response groups
result: Global work index (GWI) differed between exaggerated (2147) and normal (2036) blood pressure response groups, p<.001; other myocardial work parameters not significantly different. Clinical/physiological study, not a software usability study.

title: A Wavelet-Based Approach for Motion Artifact Reduction in Ambulatory Seismocardiography.
venue: IEEE journal of translational engineering in health and medicine
metric: Heart-rate estimation accuracy (R-squared) from motion-corrupted SCG at set SNR
result: Algorithm (MODWT + time-frequency masking + NMF) improved heart-rate estimation from R^2 0.1 to 0.8 at -15 dB SNR; reduced motion artifacts up to -19 dB SNR without ECG reference.

title: Feasibility of self-measurement telemonitoring using a handheld heart sound recorder in patients with heart failure - SELPH multicenter pilot study.
metric: Self-measurement adherence rate and patient usability questionnaire
result: Self-measurement rate >70% of days in 75% of patients; 87% of patients found self-telemonitoring helpful; 96% could use the devices without cohabitant support.

title: BrainBeats as an Open-Source EEGLAB Plugin to Jointly Analyze EEG and Cardiovascular Signals.
result: Introduces the open-source BrainBeats EEGLAB plugin (GUI and command line) for joint EEG/HRV feature extraction and heart-artifact removal from EEG; no quantitative evaluation results reported in the abstract.

title: Detection of focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures using a connected shirt.
metric: Sensitivity, false alarm rate, and ROC-AUC for seizure detection from ECG/accelerometer
result: Sensitivity 84.8% (56/66 seizures), median FAR 0.55/24 h, ROC-AUC 0.90 (95% CI 0.88-0.91), median detection latency 25.5 s.

title: KardiaMobile 6L versus 12-lead ECG: Effects on clinic utilization time.
task_time: room utilization time: 7.27 +/- 1.93 min (6L) vs 10.33 +/- 2.2 min (12L), p<.001
error_rate: 16% (8/50) of 6L visits required an additional 12-lead ECG
metric: Clinic room utilization time comparing KardiaMobile 6L to standard 12-lead ECG
result: Room utilization time significantly lower with KardiaMobile 6L (7.27 min) than 12-lead ECG (10.33 min), p<.001; 16% of 6L visits needed a follow-up 12-lead ECG.

title: Robust fatigue markers obtained from muscle synergy analysis.
result: Muscle-synergy biomarkers (activation phase difference, coactivation area/time) tracked fatigue during leg-press exercise; ECG used only as an ancillary physiological signal, not a cardiology software study.

title: DR.BEAT: Rule-Based Algorithm for SCG Analysis Without ECG Reference.
venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
metric: Heartbeat detection rate of a rule-based SCG algorithm without ECG reference
result: 87.6% of heartbeats detected overall; 97.6% at rest; 71.9% during physical stress, across 12 heart-healthy adults.

title: Evaluation of a New Mobile Virtual Reality Setup to Alter Pain Perception: Pilot Development and Usability Study in Healthy Participants.
metric: Usability (5-point scale) and simulator-sickness questionnaire scores for a mobile cardiovisual VR setup
result: Mean usability score 4.42/5 (SD 0.56) and mean simulator sickness 1.18/4 (SD 0.46); no significant effect of synchronous vs. asynchronous cardiovisual stimulation on pain perception or ownership.

title: Successful Rescue of Ventricular Fibrillation Electrical Storm Secondary to Acute Myocardial Infarction in a Patient Presenting to a District General Hospital: A Case Report.
result: Single-patient case report of successful resuscitation and PCI treatment of an electrical storm following STEMI; clinical case management, not a software study.

title: ECG-LM: Understanding Electrocardiogram with a Large Language Model.
result: Abstract not available; title indicates development of a large language model for ECG interpretation. No extractable data.

title: Monitoring heart rhythms in adult males with X-linked ichthyosis using wearable technology: a feasibility study.
metric: Data return rate and diagnostic yield of Apple Watch ECG monitoring in a rare-disease cohort
result: >95% data return rate over 8 weeks; 2/5 participants showed ventricular ectopic beats; the single watch 'alert' ECG returned was read as normal sinus rhythm (possible false positive).

title: An Explainable AI Application (AF'fective) to Support Monitoring of Patients With Atrial Fibrillation After Catheter Ablation: Qualitative Focus Group, Design Session, and Interview Study.
metric: Qualitative user-experience evaluation of an explainable-AI prototype by cardiologists
result: Progressive web app prototype received above-average user experience evaluations from cardiologists in a 3-stage co-design/pilot process; no numeric score reported.

title: Screening for Left Ventricular Hypertrophy Using Artificial Intelligence Algorithms Based on 12 Leads of the Electrocardiogram-Applicable in Clinical Practice?-Critical Literature Review with Meta-Analysis.
result: Abstract not available; title indicates a critical literature review with meta-analysis of AI algorithms screening for left ventricular hypertrophy on 12-lead ECG. No extractable data.

title: Feasibility of Remote Intensive Monitoring: A Novel Approach to Reduce Black Postpartum Maternal Cardiovascular Complications.
metric: Feasibility, acceptability, appropriateness and usability (System Usability Scale) of remote postpartum monitoring
result: Rated feasible 93%, acceptable 93%, appropriate 92%, usable 80% (SUS); remote monitoring detected 60% of women with BP >140/90 mmHg in the first 2 postpartum weeks.

title: Physiological Sensors Equipped in Wearable Devices for Management of Long COVID Persisting Symptoms: Scoping Review.
result: PRISMA-ScR scoping review of 11 studies (of 1186 screened) on wearables for long COVID; 10 different devices identified (4 FDA-approved) covering HRV, temperature, sleep and activity; narrative synthesis without a single comparable usability/performance figure.

title: Advanced ECG Analysis to Evaluate Multimodal Exercise Effects on Cardiovascular Health.
result: Abstract not available; title indicates advanced ECG analysis of multimodal exercise effects on cardiovascular health. No extractable data.

title: A Moroccan Experience in the Management of Acute Coronary Syndrome Without ST-Segment Elevation: Clinical Profiles and Therapeutic Approaches.
metric: Clinical, paraclinical and therapeutic profile of NSTEMI patients
result: Retrospective single-center cohort of 140 NSTEMI patients; in-hospital mortality 3%; clinical epidemiology study, not a software study.

title: Effects of anthropomorphic features of co-robots on users' perception and emotional responses during human-robot collaboration.
result: Human-robot collaboration study on robot appearance/voice effects on user perception, using ECG/GSR/eye-tracking as physiological measures; not a cardiology software study.

title: False Crisis Alarms in Cardiopulmonary Monitoring:: Identification, Causes, and Clinical Implications.
venue: Critical care nursing clinics of North America
metric: Classification of true vs. false crisis alarms in cardiopulmonary monitoring
result: Among crisis alarms reviewed, 11 true ventricular tachycardia and 11 true asystole alarms were identified; a high number of false alarms attributed to artifacts and low QRS voltage.

title: Advancing emotion recognition with Virtual Reality: A multimodal approach using physiological signals and machine learning.
metric: Machine-learning classification accuracy for emotion recognition from multimodal physiological signals
result: ML models reached 80%, 85% and 70% accuracy for arousal, valence and 4-class emotion classification respectively; ECG used only as one of several affective-computing signals, not a cardiology software study.

title: The inverse and non-linear association between central augmentation index and heart rate variability in a cohort of male British combat personnel- findings from the ADVANCE study.
result: Cohort analysis (ADVANCE study) of male British combat veterans finding lower HRV (RMSSD) associated with higher central augmentation index; physiological association study, not a software study.

title: Software for Analysis of Heart Rate and Blood Pressure Time-series Data from the Valsalva Maneuver.
result: Describes ValsalvaAnalyzer, a MATLAB GUI software combining signal processing and modeling to extract over 35 HR/BP biomarkers from Valsalva maneuver data; no user-study or performance metrics reported in the abstract.

title: Classifying social and physical pain from multimodal physiological signals using machine learning.
metric: Machine-learning accuracy for classifying pain type from multimodal physiological signals
result: ML classifiers reached 0.82 accuracy for social pain and 0.90 for physical pain vs. baseline; 0.63-0.77 accuracy distinguishing pain types; ECG used only as one of several signals, not a cardiology software study.

title: A homecare in-bed hardware system for precise real-time ECG and HRV monitoring with layered clothing.
metric: Electrode noise performance of a contactless in-bed ECG/HRV sensing system
result: Flexible active electrodes achieved 64 dB noise reduction via double active shielding, with input-referred noise of 0.49 uV (abstract truncated before further results).

title: The effectiveness and user preferences of two tactile breathing devices in reducing stress in stressed individuals: A mixed methods study.
venue: International journal of clinical and health psychology : IJCHP
metric: Physiological stress markers (EEG power, HR, HRV, respiration) and user preference between two tactile breathing devices
result: No significant difference in mean HR between devices; HRV decreased with both during use; moonbird produced more sustained EEG/respiratory effects and was preferred overall for handling and breathing guidance (no preference or effect-size numbers reported)

title: Cognitive Load Prediction From Multimodal Physiological Signals Using Multiview Learning.
venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
metric: Three-class cognitive load classification accuracy from multimodal physiological signals (EEG, EDA, ECG, EOG, eye movements) during flight-relevant tasks
result: Average classification accuracy 81.08% and F1-score 80.94% across 22 participants using a multiview feature-selection framework

title: Assessment of Drivers' Mental Workload by Multimodal Measures during Auditory-Based Dual-Task Driving Scenarios.
metric: Mental workload assessment via subjective, physiological (EEG, ECG, EDA, eye movement), and driving-performance measures during simulated dual-task driving
result: Increasing secondary-task difficulty raised subjective workload and reduced secondary-task performance; ECG time/frequency-domain measures and other physiological/driving indices showed workload-related changes (no effect sizes reported)

title: Heart rate response to cognitive load as a marker of depression and increased anxiety.
metric: Association between ECG/PPG-derived heart rate response to a cognitive 1-back task and depression/anxiety severity
result: Task accuracy decreased with difficulty; heart-rate increases under cognitive load were associated with higher depression/trait-anxiety (PPG) and with anxiety attacks (ECG), an association that weakened at higher difficulty (no effect sizes reported)

title: Rapid Mental Workload Detection of Air Traffic Controllers with Three EEG Sensors.
metric: Mental workload detection accuracy from a 3-channel EEG (gamma-band) model in air traffic controllers, using mRMR channel selection
result: Detection rate of 1.0 for 34 subjects and accuracy as low as 0.986 for the remaining subjects (total sample size not stated)

title: Heart rate variability as a dynamic marker of surgeons' stress during vascular surgery.
metric: Correlation between intraoperative heart rate variability and surgeons' self-reported stress (STAI-6) during vascular surgery
result: HRV indicated greater stress at key procedural points across 11 surgeons; HRV correlated with subjective stress (r=0.768, p<0.001)

title: Lessons learned from a multimodal sensor-based eHealth approach for treating pediatric obsessive-compulsive disorder.
metric: Feasibility and usability of a multimodal sensor-based (eye-tracking, ECG chest strap, motion) eHealth intervention for pediatric OCD therapy
result: Technology was well accepted; patients, parents, and therapists reported high satisfaction and fewer OCD symptoms at treatment end (no numeric satisfaction score reported)

title: Safety, feasibility, and acceptability of a novel device to monitor ischaemic stroke patients.
error_rate: 0 adverse events reported (0/17 patients) over 9 hours of device wear
metric: Safety (adverse events), feasibility (data capture), and acceptability (comfort/satisfaction) of a wearable EEG/ECG device for monitoring ischaemic stroke patients
result: No adverse events among 17 patients wearing the device for 9 hours, only minor discomfort; comfort and data-capture feasibility were assessed at 1, 3, 6, and 9 hours but exact values are not present in this abstract excerpt

title: Assessment of Physiological Signals from Photoplethysmography Sensors Compared to an Electrocardiogram Sensor: A Validation Study in Daily Life.
error_rate: Mean absolute error <1 bpm (HR) and 6-15 ms (HRV); HRV relative error 14-51% higher during activity than at rest
metric: Accuracy of PPG-derived heart rate (HR) and heart rate variability (HRV) versus an ECG reference sensor in free-living conditions
result: Mean absolute error <1 bpm for HR and 6-15 ms for HRV; PPG HRV error 14-51% higher during activity than rest; peak-detection F1 score of 89% during sleep, across 25 volunteers monitored for 10 days

title: Utilization of a hierarchical electrocardiogram classification model for enhanced biometric identification.
metric: Accuracy of a 2-stage hierarchical ECG classification model for biometric user identification across varying stress states
result: Identification accuracy of 92.08% (CSU-BIODB) and 95.83% (MIT-BIH ST Change database); F1 scores of 0.9207 and 0.9369; 9.3% and 36.76% accuracy improvement over single-stage baseline models

title: Citrus Odour Produces Resilient Response to Cognitive Load and Enhances Performance in the N-Back Task.
metric: Effect of citrus odour on cognitive performance (2-back task) and autonomic measures (ECG/HRV, PPG, EDA) under cognitive load
result: Citrus odour significantly improved 2-back accuracy and suppressed the EDA rise seen under cognitive load; parasympathetic HRV measures (pNN50, RMSSD, HF power) increased, though overall HRV variability was unchanged (no effect sizes reported)

title: Multicenter Evaluation of Machine-Learning Continuous Pulse Rate Algorithm on Wrist-Worn Device.
error_rate: Accuracy root-mean-square (ARMS) of 1.67 bpm under no-motion conditions
metric: Accuracy of a machine-learning wrist-worn PPG continuous pulse-rate algorithm versus a reference ECG device
result: ARMS of 1.67 bpm under no-motion conditions across 16,915 paired observations from 157 subjects in 3 clinical trials, meeting the pre-specified acceptance thresholds (<=3 bpm no-motion, <=5 bpm motion)

title: A deep learning modular ECG approach for cardiologist assisted adjudication of atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter episodes.
metric: Accuracy of a deep-learning modular ECG algorithm, with a cardiologist-adjudication interface, for atrial fibrillation/flutter detection on long-term Holter recordings
result: F1 scores of 99% (atrial tachyarrhythmia), 95% (atrial fibrillation), and 90% (atrial flutter) on 187 internal recordings (249,419 samples); external MIT-BIH validation F1 97% (normal sinus rhythm) and 96% (tachyarrhythmia); residual errors correctable by manual module deactivation in 7 of 15 lower-accuracy recordings

title: Heart rate variability is more sensitive to stress than heart rate in specialist police undergoing selection.
metric: Correlation between heart rate variability (pRR50%) and aerobic fitness (20 m shuttle test) versus heart rate alone, during police tactical selection
result: pRR50% significantly correlated with shuttle-test performance (rho=0.812, p=0.050); heart rate alone was not significantly correlated with fitness or predictive of task performance, across a cohort of 6 candidates

title: Photoplethysmography-based HRV analysis and machine learning for real-time stress quantification in mental health applications.
metric: Correlation of PPG-derived RR intervals with ECG reference, and correlation of a PPG-based ML stress model's score with a validated stress questionnaire (DASS-21-C)
result: PPG-ECG RR interval correlation r=0.9920, R2=0.9837; ML stress model baseline score vs DASS-21-C stress score correlation r=0.92, R2=0.8457

title: Evaluation of Telemetric Single-Lead Cardiac Transmitter and Apple Watch for Heart Rate Monitoring: Implications for Heart Failure Management in Home Care.
error_rate: MAPE 2.39-3.30% (Cocoron) vs 2.26-5.82% (Apple Watch 7) across supine/seated/walking positions
metric: Heart rate measurement accuracy of a telemetric single-lead ECG transmitter and Apple Watch 7 versus an RF-ECG reference, across postures
result: MAPE of 2.39%/3.30%/3.27% (Cocoron) vs 2.26%/3.71%/5.82% (Apple Watch 7) for supine/seated/walking; Cocoron significantly more accurate overall (p=0.013); Apple Watch showed larger error and wider limits of agreement during ambulation (upper LOA 12.02), attributed to PPG motion artifact

title: Can ChatGPT accurately detect atrial fibrillation using smartwatch ECG?
venue: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
metric: Diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4o versus the Apple Watch's built-in algorithm for classifying atrial fibrillation from single-lead smartwatch ECG
result: Apple Watch algorithm: 97.3% accuracy for AF and 100% for sinus rhythm; GPT-4o correctly classified 47.3% of AF and 71.6% of sinus rhythm tracings, across 114 AF patients and 60 controls

title: Systematic review of neurophysiological assessment techniques and metrics for mental workload evaluation in real-world settings.
metric: Systematic review of objective neurophysiological methods (ECG, EEG, eye data) for assessing mental workload in real-world professional settings
result: 35 studies included, showing a diversity of measurement tools often combined with subjective assessments; no unified measurement framework identified

title: fNIRS, EEG, ECG, and GSR reveal an effect of complex, dynamically changing environments on cognitive load, affective state, and performance, but not physiological stress.
metric: Effect of a complex, dynamically changing environment on cognitive load, affective state, performance, and physiological stress (fNIRS, EEG, ECG, EDA)
result: Abstract text truncated; effect on cognitive load, affective state, and performance reported, but not on physiological stress (specific values not available in this excerpt)

title: Machine learning evaluation model of pilot workload in a low-visibility environment.
metric: Machine-learning (HMM) evaluation of pilot mental workload from ECG signal indexes and NASA-TLX scale in a low-visibility flight simulator
result: Average heart rate and workload scale scores rose significantly in low-visibility conditions; pNN20, HF/LF, SD2/SD1, and HR discriminated workload levels; HMM-based model reached up to 87.5% accuracy, across 40 pilots

title: Validation of the EmotiBit wearable sensor for heart-based measures under varying workload conditions.
error_rate: HR average difference of 1-2 bpm vs reference ECG; HRV and EDA agreement insufficient by Bland-Altman ratio analysis
metric: Criterion validity of the EmotiBit PPG wearable versus a reference ECG device for heart rate (HR), HRV, and electrodermal activity during cognitive workload
result: Good agreement for HR (average difference 1-2 bpm); insufficient agreement for HRV and EDA measures compared to the reference ECG device, across 15 participants

title: Acceptance of Telemedicine by Specialists and General Practitioners in Cardiology Care: Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
metric: Survey of telemedicine acceptance, use frequency, and attitudes among cardiologists, internists, and general practitioners in cardiology care
result: 112 of 929 contacted physicians (12.1%) completed the survey; 43% never use telemedicine, 16% use it daily; 77.7% wanted to expand telemedicine use; clinical caseload differed significantly across attitude clusters (C1 vs C2 p=.03, C1 vs C3 p=.02, C2 vs C3 p<.001)

title: [Digitalization and clinical decision tools].
result: Narrative overview of digitalization in cardiovascular emergencies: prehospital digital ECG transmission, guideline/decision-support apps, and AI for image analysis and risk prediction, with regulatory and data-protection barriers discussed; no primary data reported

title: Ultra-Low Power Analog Folded Neural Network for Cardiovascular Health Monitoring.
venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
metric: Detection performance and power/space trade-offs of a batteryless analog folded neural network for ECG-based screening
result: A favorable accuracy trade-off was found around 6 layers and a hidden size of 30; feasibility of batteryless wearable implementation demonstrated (no specific accuracy percentage reported)

title: Interpretation of SPECT wall motion with deep learning.
venue: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology
task_time: DL model generated results within 30 seconds via a guided user interface
metric: Diagnostic accuracy of a deep-learning model for interpreting SPECT wall motion versus human readers and quantitative parameters (echocardiography as reference)
result: AUC 0.82 (DL) vs 0.77 (human, p<.001) vs 0.74 (quantitative parameters, p<.05); accuracy 0.88 (DL) vs 0.82 (human) vs 0.78 (quantitative); net reclassification index 7.7%, across 1038 patients

title: 3D E-textile for Exercise Physiology and Clinical Maternal Health Monitoring.
metric: Feasibility of a 3D microfiber E-textile electrode system for ECG/EMG signal acquisition during exercise and clinical maternal monitoring
result: System demonstrated low electrode-skin impedance without gel, waterproofing, and real-time multimodal ECG/EMG monitoring during cycling, swimming, and a clinical maternal ECG/EMG study (no comparative accuracy or usability numbers reported)

title: Smartphone App for Prehospital ECG Transmission in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Activation: Protocol for a Mixed Methods Study.
result: Study protocol (not yet reporting results) for evaluating a smartphone app for prehospital ECG transmission and STEMI catheterization-lab activation; planned outcomes include usability, acceptability, treatment-time intervals, and false-activation rates

title: Clinical usability of deep learning-based saliency maps for occlusion myocardial infarction identification from the prehospital 12-Lead electrocardiogram.
metric: Clinician-rated clinical relevance and helpfulness of deep-learning saliency maps for occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) identification from ECG, and diagnostic accuracy of clinicians versus the DL model
result: Clinicians' adjudicated AUC 0.855 vs DL model AUC 0.872 (F1 0.789 vs 0.747); saliency maps rated slightly clinically relevant (0.96 +/- 0.92) and slightly helpful (0.66 +/- 0.98) on a -3 to +3 Likert scale; clinician confidence in model predictions 1.71 +/- 0.56, across 100 ECGs reviewed by 3 clinicians

title: A randomized controlled implementation study integrating patient self-screening with a remote central monitoring system to screen community dwellers aged 75 years and older for atrial fibrillation.
metric: AF diagnosis rate, participant satisfaction, and device usability/feasibility (confidence, ease of use, efficiency) in self-screening vs usual care
result: AF diagnosed in 10.3% of intervention vs 2.0% of control participants (OR 5.6, 95% CI 1.4-37.3, p=0.03); 97.9% of intervention vs 59.1% of control-waitlisted participants satisfied (p<0.001); 93% confident using the device, 98% found it easy to use, 96% found screening efficient.

title: Validation and user experience of a dry electrode based Health Patch for heart rate and respiration rate monitoring.
metric: Agreement (Lin's concordance coefficient) between Health Patch and reference devices for heart rate, respiratory rate and HRV; qualitative user experience
result: Lin's CCC 0.98 for heart rate, 0.56 for respiratory rate, 0.85 for HRV (RMSSD); participants generally reported a positive experience with minor adhesive-related skin irritation.

title: Evaluating the Effects of Different Cognitive Tasks on Autonomic Nervous System Responses: Implementation of a High-Precision, Low-Cost Complementary Method.
metric: Skin conductance level, reaction time and HRV changes during cognitive tasks vs baseline, using a low-cost ECG/SCR test battery
result: Skin conductance levels and reaction times increased with cognitive load, and vagally-mediated HRV parameters changed significantly vs baseline; no specific effect-size numbers reported in the abstract.

title: Solving the Inverse Problem of Electrocardiography for Cardiac Digital Twins: A Survey.
result: Review of deterministic and probabilistic (including deep-learning) methods for solving the ECG inverse problem for cardiac digital twins; discusses validation strategies and clinical-workflow integration challenges without a single pooled quantitative outcome.

title: The UNICA sleep HRV analysis tool: an integrated open-source tool for heart rate variability analysis during sleep.
metric: Validation of the UNICA-HRV open-source MATLAB tool against established HRV tools (Kubios, PhysioZoo)
result: Described as robust and precise for generating HRV metrics compared with Kubios and PhysioZoo; no specific accuracy figures reported in the abstract.

title: Exploring the limits of scan time reduction for ferumoxytol-enhanced whole-heart angiography in congenital heart disease patients.
venue: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
task_time: Accelerated free-running MRI acquisitions reduced to 3 minutes or less (from a 6-minute baseline) while preserving diagnostic image quality
metric: Diagnostic image-quality rating (5-point Likert) and consistency of motion-state selection across undersampling levels (SIMBA vs XD-MC-SIMBA)
result: 43% (31/72) of cases showed improved quality scores with XD-MC-SIMBA vs SIMBA; 58% (7/12) of 1-minute datasets improved to good/excellent quality; scan time accelerated to 3 minutes or less while preserving diagnostic quality.

title: Wear Your Heart on Your Sleeve: Smart Textile ECG Wearables for Comfort, Integration, Signal Quality and Continuous Monitoring in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
metric: AF detection rate, signal-to-noise ratio and total analysis time of textile ECG wearables vs Holter/12-lead ECG, plus user acceptability (comfort, usability, skin effects)
result: Narrative review; comparative performance and acceptability of textile ECG devices are discussed qualitatively, with no pooled quantitative results reported in the abstract.

title: Cardiac Phase Estimation Using Deep Learning Analysis of Pulsed-Mode Projections: Toward Autonomous Cardiac CT Imaging.
error_rate: <6% RMSE in cardiac phase estimation (phase range 0-100%)
metric: Cardiac phase estimation accuracy (RMSE) of PhaseNet vs competing methods, toward ECG-gating-free autonomous cardiac CT
result: ~50% RMSE improvement vs standard CNN-LSTM and ~24% vs a multi-channel residual network; the added uncertainty-driven Viterbi regularizer gave a further ~14% RMSE improvement, reaching <6% RMSE overall.

title: Value of Artificial Intelligence for Enhancing Suspicion of Cardiac Amyloidosis Using Electrocardiography and Echocardiography: A Narrative Review.
venue: Journal of the American Heart Association
metric: AI model diagnostic performance (AUC, sensitivity, specificity) for cardiac amyloidosis from ECG/echocardiography, across 13 included studies
result: AUC 0.71-1.00, sensitivity 16%-100%, specificity 75%-100% across 13 studies (n=50-2451 patients); only 4 studies included external validation; usability, cost and interoperability cited as adoption barriers.

title: A multicenter pragmatic implementation study of AI-ECG-based clinical decision support software to identify low LVEF: Clinical trial design and methods.
venue: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
metric: Trial design/methods paper; primary outcome will be detection of LVEF <=40% by echocardiography among clinical encounters exposed to EHR-integrated ECG-AI CDSS vs usual care
result: Protocol paper for a multicenter cluster-randomized trial across 5 health systems, recruiting clinicians and covering >32,000 eligible clinical encounters with 90-day follow-up; no outcome results reported yet.

title: Investigating the Use of Electrooculography Sensors to Detect Stress During Working Activities.
metric: ML classification accuracy for occupational stress detection using EOG signals
result: Random Forest reached 85.8% (2-class) and 82.4% (3-class) accuracy classifying stress from EOG signals captured via smart eyewear in 12 subjects; an occupational human-factors study unrelated to cardiology software.

title: Infusion Therapy Nursing Team: Implementation and Effectiveness of Initial Results.
venue: Journal of infusion nursing : the official publication of the Infusion Nurses Society
metric: PICC insertion outcomes of a nurse-led infusion therapy team, using intracavitary ECG for tip navigation
result: First-year report: 1502 activities including 896 PICC insertions with 81.7% first-attempt success (intracavitary ECG used only as a navigation aid); a nursing-service report, not a cardiology software study.

title: Single-lead electrocardiograms and artificial intelligence for managing cardiac rhythm irregularities in general practice: A French general practitioners' survey.
metric: French GP survey on acceptability and utility of a single-lead ECG device with AI interpretation and a decision tree for arrhythmia management
result: 221/1102 GPs responded; 44% owned an ECG device; 77% believed single-lead ECG would simplify use; 72% would use ECG more often with AI interpretation; decision-tree relevance rated 8/10.

title: A web-based system for real-time ECG monitoring using MySQL database and DigiMesh technology: design and implementation.
result: Describes the architecture of a wireless (DigiMesh) ECG monitoring system with MySQL cloud storage and web-based display for remote patient monitoring; no formal evaluation or performance metrics reported in the abstract.

title: An Electrocardiogram Foundation Model Built on over 10 Million Recordings.
metric: AUROC of the ECGFounder foundation model across diagnoses on internal/external validation, and fine-tuned performance vs baseline models
result: AUROC >0.95 for 80 diagnoses on internal validation with strong generalization on external sets; fine-tuned model outperformed baseline methods by 3-5 AUROC points across demographic analysis, clinical event detection, and cross-modality rhythm diagnosis.

title: A pediatric telecardiology system that facilitates integration between hospital-based services and community-based primary care.
error_rate: connection problems reported by 2.8% of respondents; reliability concerns by 3.7%
metric: Technical success rate of ECG transmission/reporting and user-experience survey for a pediatric telecardiology system
result: 158 children screened; ECG transmission and reporting completed successfully in all cases; 90% of respondents were very satisfied or satisfied; 70.8% of respondents completed the full survey.

title: Assessment of novel electrophysiology simulator-a survey study.
metric: Survey-based assessment of realism, usability and educational value of an online EP training simulator
result: 90% rated ECG signal realism excellent/very good (82.5% for intracardiac signals); 97.5% would include it in EP training programs; 100% would recommend it.

title: The use of cognitive load theory to assist in the teaching of electrocardiogram interpretation within paramedical science education.
result: Conceptual/opinion article applying cognitive load theory to teaching ECG interpretation in paramedical education; no empirical data reported.

title: Detection of arousal and valence from facial expressions and physiological responses evoked by different types of stressors.
metric: Classification accuracy of arousal/valence detection models using video, ECG and EDA data
result: Video-physio models distinguished high/low arousal and valence better than unimodal models, and arousal was classified better than valence; no specific accuracy percentages given. Affective-computing study using ECG only as an ancillary signal, not a cardiology software study.

title: Research on identification of flight cadets' cognitive load based on multi-source physiological data and CGAN-DBN model.
metric: Accuracy of a CGAN-DBN model identifying flight cadets' cognitive load from multi-source physiological data (eye movement, ECG, respiration)
result: Model reported to achieve 'high accuracy' for cognitive-load identification; no specific accuracy value given in the abstract. Aviation human-factors study using ECG as one of several ancillary signals, not a cardiology software study.

title: Low-cost portable EEG device for bridging the diagnostic gap in resource-limited areas.
venue: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
devices: low-cost portable EEG system (27-channel EEG + ECG)
metric: SUS and signal-quality assessment of a low-cost, app-guided portable EEG system used by inexperienced users
result: SUS score 90.3 +/- 6.8 reported by 10 inexperienced users, with an average signal-quality rating of 8.04 and no recordings of insufficient quality; this evaluates an EEG epilepsy-diagnosis system (ECG is only an accompanying channel), not cardiology software.

title: WACARDIA: Graphical MATLAB software for Wireless Assessment of CARDiac Interoceptive Accuracy.
result: Describes WACARDIA, free open-source MATLAB/Psychtoolbox software for the heartbeat-detection interoceptive-accuracy task, with a wireless-ECG interface, GUIs, and measurement fail-safes; no quantitative usability or accuracy results reported in the abstract.

title: Assessing operator stress in collaborative robotics: A multimodal approach.
metric: Alignment between physiological parameters (EEG, ECG/HRV, GSR) and subjective stress (NASA-TLX) during cobot programming tasks
result: Highest alignment with subjective stress: EEG Theta 76.67%, GSR recovery time 72.86%, HRV PNN25 71.58%; raw RR intervals were least accurate (42.11%). Human-robot collaboration ergonomics study, not a cardiology software study.

title: Usability of simplified audiometry and electrocardiogram during treatment of drug-resistant tuberculosis in Mozambique: a qualitative study.
metric: Qualitative themes on usability of simplified ECG and audiometry devices among healthcare providers and DR-TB patients
result: 16 healthcare providers and 91 people with drug-resistant tuberculosis were interviewed; providers understood the importance of ECG monitoring but lacked confidence managing the devices and interpreting results; limited device numbers and training were cited as barriers.

title: Cardiac Function and Fatigue During Exoskeleton-Assisted Sit-to-Stand Maneuver and Walking in People with Stroke with Moderate to Severe Gait Disability: A Pilot Cross-Sectional Study.
metric: Cardiac function (heart rate, R-R interval from ECG) and workload (NASA-TLX) during exoskeleton-assisted gait vs walking without exoskeleton
result: No significant difference in heart rate/R-R ECG data across conditions; NASA-TLX largely unchanged except one comparison. Exoskeleton rehabilitation study using ECG as a safety measure, not a cardiology software study.

title: Takeover performance prediction model considering cognitive load: analysis of subjective and objective factors.
metric: Improvement in driver takeover-performance prediction accuracy (GA-BP vs BP neural network) using eye-movement and ECG data
result: At the 10 s time window, the GA-BP model improved accuracy by 5.51%, recall by 7.08%, precision by 6.19% and F1 by 9.71% vs the baseline model. Driving-simulation human-factors study using ECG as an ancillary signal, not a cardiology software study.

title: Can heart rate variability demonstrate progression of mindfulness through two-week repeated practice?
venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
metric: Change in HRV metrics (parasympathetic activity) across two weeks of mindfulness practice, experienced (n=20) vs novice (n=26) practitioners
result: Experienced practitioners showed significantly increased, stable parasympathetic activity across practice; novices showed high cognitive load with inconspicuous progressive effects; no specific HRV values reported. A mindfulness/psychophysiology study, not a cardiology software study.

title: A Pilot Study of the Home-Based 12-Lead Electrocardiogram in Clinical Practice.
venue: Mayo Clinic proceedings. Innovations, quality & outcomes
task_time: median 51 minutes per telephone appointment with an ECG technician; average 2.2 attempts to record a usable ECG
error_rate: 2/10 patients unable to obtain a diagnostic-quality ECG
metric: Feasibility and efficiency of home-based 12-lead ECG acquisition prior to a telehealth cardiology appointment
result: 8/10 patients obtained a diagnostic-quality ECG; median technician call time 51 minutes; average 2.2 attempts needed; barriers included internet access, training materials, and motion artifact.

title: Usability and acceptability of ambulatory monitoring in undiagnosed syncope: insights from the ASPIRED-Q qualitative study.
metric: Qualitative usability and acceptability themes from semi-structured interviews
result: Patients found the patch non-obstructive and easy to use; healthcare professionals found attachment simple but noted added documentation time and training needs; device was positively received overall

title: Tracing Visual Expertise in ECG Interpretation: An Eye-Tracking Pilot Study.
venue: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
task_time: Experts 107.6 ± 32.8 s vs residents 205.31 ± 57.43 s per ECG (p<0.001)
metric: ECG interpretation time, diagnostic accuracy, eye-tracking fixations, pupil dilation, NASA-TLX cognitive load
result: Experts read ECGs faster and more accurately than residents, with fewer but longer fixations, lower pupil dilation, and higher self-assessed performance (all p<0.05)

ECG interpretation abilities in clinical practice: Examining the role of expertise, age, and gender.
metric: Diagnostic accuracy in ECG interpretation across expertise levels; Random Forest classification accuracy
result: Cardiology consultants showed the highest diagnostic accuracy; younger participants (26-30) outperformed older groups; males had higher recognition rates; targeted educational interventions improved accuracy; a Random Forest model reached 81% accuracy classifying long vs short ECG readings

The accuracy of Gemini, GPT-4, and GPT-4o in ECG analysis: A comparison with cardiologists and emergency medicine specialists.
venue: The American journal of emergency medicine
metric: Diagnostic accuracy of LLMs (GPT-4, GPT-4o, Gemini Advanced) vs cardiologists and emergency medicine specialists in ECG interpretation; inter-rater agreement (Fleiss Kappa)
result: Cardiologists outperformed all three LLMs; GPT-4o outperformed Gemini Advanced (p=0.004) and GPT-4 (p<0.001) on routine ECGs and outperformed both overall; agreement was weak for GPT-4 (kappa=0.265) and Gemini Advanced (kappa=0.347), moderate for GPT-4o (kappa=0.514)

title: Validity, Accuracy, and Safety Assessment of an Aerobic Interval Training Using an App-Based Prehabilitation Program (PROTEGO MAXIMA Trial) Before Major Surgery: Prospective, Interventional Pilot Study.
error_rate: Mean heart rate difference ≤5 bpm; mean absolute percentage error ≤5% vs standard ECG
metric: Accuracy and safety of app-based wearable heart rate measurement vs standard ECG and treadmill; usability and alarm-signal testing; adverse event rate
result: Mean heart rate difference ≤5 bpm and mean absolute percentage error ≤5% vs standard ECG in 75 participants; 39% experienced mild adverse events (skin irritation, dizziness, fatigue) with no serious device deficiencies

title: WHICH DEVICE IS MOST SUITABLE FOR MEASURING HEART RATE VARIABILITY IN THE FIELD? A COMPARATIVE EVALUATION OF TWO LEADING OPTIONS.
venue: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
metric: Comparative device usability and feasibility for HRV monitoring (literature review, device testing, expert interviews)
result: Polar H10 is affordable and records RR intervals up to 20 hours offline but needs a smartwatch/app for extended storage; Bittium Faros is a certified ECG monitor recording full waveforms with automatic data transfer; both require chest straps with possible placement or skin issues

title: The cognitive impacts of large language model interactions on problem solving and decision making using EEG analysis.
